chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Husayn ibn Ishaq, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid and Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, all from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, who said:
I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asking him a question, so he wrote to me:

Surely the hypocrites strive to deceive Allah, and He shall Requite their deceit back to them, and when they stand up for the Prayer they stand up sluggishly; they do it only to be seen of men and do not remember Allah except for a little
Wavering between that (and this), (belonging) neither to these nor to those; and whomsoever Allah Causes to err, you shall not find a way for him

They are neither from the Unbelievers nor from the Believers, and they are not from the Muslims. They are displaying the Faith and they are becoming to the Disbelief and (with) the lies. May Allah Curse them
ai.seo_question: What distinguishes the hypocrites from believers and disbelievers in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) elaborates on the spiritual state of the *munafiqun* by linking their behavioral traits—such as sluggishness in prayer and *riya'* (showing off)—to the Quranic description of being 'wavering' (*mudhabdhibin*). It emphasizes their unique ontological status as a distinct group separate from both *kuffar* and * mu'minun*, characterized by a gradual internal shift from faith to denial while maintaining an outward facade of Islam.
